faqs.q: What causes fascia to rot on a Bloomfield home?

runs.v: Water: clogged and overflowing gutters back up and soak the board, and loose gutters leave a gap that lets water reach the fascia, per InterNACHI inspection guidance.

faqs.q: How do I know if my Bloomfield fascia needs replacing?

runs.v: Peeling or blistering paint, soft and spongy spots, cracks and flaking, and gutters sagging or pulling from the roofline; the worst rot often hides behind the gutter.

faqs.q: What fascia material lasts longest on a Bloomfield home?

runs.v: Aluminum, PVC, and fiber-cement fascia resist rot longer than painted wood, which typically lasts roughly 15–25 years and needs a repaint cycle. Aluminum fascia carries a 20-to-40-plus-year life, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, while PVC shrugs off water and fiber-cement resists water and insects.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace fascia in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: Usually not: fascia replacement does not usually require a local permit for a like-for-like installation, and trim and roof-covering repair on a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Commercial, multi-family, attached, and historic-district properties can need a permit or extra review, so confirm current requirements with the Bloomfield construction office first.
